exercises.name: Frog Rock
exercises.note: Tennis and padel ask your groin for more range than almost any other sport. Every wide ball, every open-stance forehand, every lunge to the net is an adductor at length under load. This session trains that range instead of hoping you have it when the ball arrives.

good: On all fours, knees wide, feet turned out in line with the knees
Rock the hips back slowly until you feel the groin, then come forward
Keep the lower back flat. When it starts to round, that is your end range
bad: Bouncing at the back of the rock
Widening the knees past what you can control

good: On all fours, one leg out straight to the side, foot flat
Rock back and feel it down the inside of the straight leg
Slow. Let the range open over the ten rather than forcing the first one
bad: Letting the straight leg's foot roll onto its edge

exercises.name: Cossack Squat
exercises.note: This is the closest thing in the gym to a wide defensive ball. You are strong in the bottom of it or you are not, and if you are not, that is the position where a groin tears. Bodyweight only, hands out in front for balance, and hold a chair if you need it.

good: Wide stance, sit down over one leg with the other straight
Heel of the bent leg stays down. Turn the straight foot up if it helps
Go only as deep as you can come back up from without a wobble
bad: Dropping in and using a bounce to get out
Letting the bent knee cave inwards

good: Step wide, sit into that hip, reach both hands past the outside of the foot
Push back out through the heel to stand
This is the same shape as the Cossack but moving, so it should feel easier
bad: Staying upright. The reach is what makes the hip work

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Hip Flexor with Overhead Reach
exercises.note: Hours in a low ready stance leave the front of the hip short, and a short hip flexor quietly steals range from everything above it. Squeezing the back glute is what makes this a stretch of the hip rather than a stretch of your lower back.

good: Half-kneeling, squeeze the back glute first, then reach the same-side arm overhead
Ribs down. Tuck the tailbone under before you reach
Add a small lean away from the kneeling side for the last fifteen seconds
bad: Arching the lower back to feel more
Pushing the hips forward without the glute squeeze

good: Sit into the bottom of a squat, elbows inside the knees, gently push them out
Hold a door frame if your heels lift
Breathe and let it settle. Shift side to side if you want more
